clue.text: Paper-weight?

parts.note: read literally, a weight that holds a sail (a sheet) in place, a big emergency anchor; also a sheet of paper plus a heavy weight

explanation.walkthrough: The desk object is a decoy: split it as a sheet (paper) and an anchor (weight). The term is also used for a dependable person or last resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's largest anchor, kept for emergencies, and by extension any mainstay one relies on in a crisis.

clue.text: Discover successful record, two-thirds of one!

parts.note: a chart-topping single is called a hit

indicators.note: the word one has three letters, and this asks for its leading two of the three

explanation.surface: Someone finds a chart success that is, oddly, only two-thirds of a single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds of' takes the first two of the three letters of 'one', giving ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on something is an idiom for to stumble upon or find it.

clue.text: Way out I leave unmannerly, squeeze out

indicators.note: leave here means to drop or let go, so the letter I is taken out of the exit word

parts.note: a way out is an exit
unmannerly means rude

explanation.surface: Someone rudely pushes their way out of an exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' tells you to remove I from EXIT, giving EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to force or press material out through an opening.

clue.text: State in the manner of knight in south Africa

parts.note: from the French phrase à la, meaning in the style of

indicators.note: in here means placed inside, so knight sits within the abbreviation for South Africa

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for knight, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A description of a knight behaving in a certain style somewhere in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts K inside SA to give SKA.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state, the largest in the Union, bought from Russia in 1867.

clue.text: Commander-in-chief on the Yorkshire river found belt

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means sitting above, so the commander's letters come before the rest

parts.note: commonly abbreviated C-in-C
in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t', as in 'on t' moor'
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A military chief standing by a northern river discovers a belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' gives T because Yorkshire speech clips it to t', and 'Yorkshire' does double duty in the surface to hint at that; the Ure flows through Wensleydale.
explanation.definitionFit: A cincture is a girdle or band worn round the waist, especially over a cleric's vestment.

clue.text: Lubricate outer covering on raincoat

parts.note: to lubricate is to oil
skin is the outer covering of a body or fruit

explanation.surface: Someone oils the outer layer of their waterproof.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat made of cloth treated with oil to keep out the wet, worn by fishermen.

clue.text: It takes turns to produce a yarn

definitions.text: It takes turns to produce a yarn

parts.words: It takes turns to produce a yarn
parts.note: reads like a storyteller taking turns at spinning a tale, but describes a rotating device that twists fibre into thread

explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' suggests a tale and 'takes turns' suggests sharing, but the turns are revolutions and the yarn is thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic machine with a large wheel, rotated by hand or foot, used to twist wool or flax into thread.

clue.text: Was taken in having confessed

definitions.meaning: was allowed to enter, as a patient to a hospital

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both being let into a place such as hospital and having acknowledged guilt.

clue.text: Landing gear below coach

parts.note: below means under
a railway coach is a carriage

explanation.surface: Aircraft wheels sit beneath a passenger coach.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheels and supporting struts beneath an aircraft that bear it on the ground.

clue.text: Bad temper it followed was insignificant

indicators.note: followed means the word it comes after the temper word in the answer

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or peevishness, as in 'in a pet'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bout of sulking that came afterwards turned out to be trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit, from French for small, means minor or petty, as in petit larceny.

clue.text: It's to do with worms that lady confused Daniel

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the name Daniel are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman bewilders a man named Daniel by talking about worms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges DANIEL into ELIDAN, placed after ANN.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for the segmented worm phylum, which includes earthworms and leeches.

clue.text: Same lady performed flourish on trumpet in eastern USA

indicators.note: performed here means worked over or acted upon, so the three letters of the lady's name are rearranged

parts.note: the woman from the previous clue, Ann
a tucket is an old word for a trumpet fanfare, found in Shakespeare's stage directions

explanation.surface: The same woman gave a fanfare on a trumpet somewhere on the American east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' turns ANN into NAN. TUCKET is an archaic word for a trumpet flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantucket is an island off Massachusetts, a place found on the eastern seaboard of the US.

clue.text: Potassium, nickel and iron blade

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A list of metals making up a cutting edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tool consisting of a sharp edge set in a handle.

clue.text: Fashionable food said to be natural

parts.note: in means in fashion

indicators.note: said signals that the word for food is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: bread is a staple food

explanation.surface: A trendy loaf is claimed to be wholesome and natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbred qualities are innate, part of one's nature from birth.

clue.text: Security provided by fellows who are stewards

indicators.note: by means next to, so the fellows' letters stand beside the provided word

parts.note: bail is money given as security for a released prisoner
provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'
F is the abbreviation for fellow; adding S makes it plural

explanation.surface: Guarantees given by members of a college who also run the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: FS is a pluralised abbreviation, the letter F for fellow plus S. 'who are' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff is a landowner's agent or steward who manages an estate.

clue.text: Entire reorganisation in football club was wildly frantic

indicators.note: in here means placed inside, so the rearranged letters sit within the club abbreviation
reorganisation means the letters of Entire are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A complete shake-up at a football club caused frenzied activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganisation' turns ENTIRE into RENETI, and 'in' puts that between F and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means frenzied, marked by wild, uncontrolled excitement or haste.

clue.text: Coming from Lochaber, he is not in a union

definitions.text: he is not in a union

indicators.note: coming from here means made out of, so the letters of the place name are reworked

explanation.surface: A Highland man from Lochaber who has never married.
explanation.walkthrough: Lochaber is a district of the Scottish Highlands; its eight letters rearrange exactly. 'Coming from' looks like a statement of origin but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man, one not joined in wedlock.

clue.text: Achieving success in the long run

definitions.text: Achieving success in the long run

parts.words: Achieving success in the long run
parts.note: reads as eventual success, but literally describes covering a long distance on a run

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the long run' looks like 'eventually', but it can also be read as travelling a great distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means likely to be very successful in one's career, as in 'that youngster will go far'.

clue.text: Travel to old city having faced gastronome

parts.note: to travel is to go
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite
met means confronted or faced

explanation.surface: A traveller heads to an ancient city and comes face to face with a food lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a connoisseur of fine food and drink, as is a gastronome.

clue.text: One engaged in business on ship

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who buys and sells and a merchant vessel used in commerce.

clue.text: As many as can be put in saloon perhaps

definitions.text: As many as can be put in saloon perhaps

parts.words: As many as can be put in saloon perhaps
parts.note: a saloon is a kind of room, so this is the quantity a room can hold

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' might suggest a car or a bar, but it is just an example of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount or number of people or things a room will hold.

clue.text: Cut part with dry interior

indicators.note: interior means the dry word goes on the inside of the part word

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece
sec is French for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: A bit of something with a dry centre is sliced through.
explanation.walkthrough: SEC, a wine-list word for dry, sits inside BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal parts.

clue.text: In Shanghai, kudos for Japanese verse

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A Chinese city gives praise to a short poem from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'Shanghai' and the start of 'kudos'.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a three-line poem of seventeen syllables in the Japanese tradition.

clue.text: Greek mass

parts.note: suggests a church service in Greece but means a Greek phrase for the common people

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' tempts one towards an Orthodox church service; it is the masses, named by a Greek phrase meaning 'the many'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek phrase, literally 'the many', used in English for the common people or the masses.

clue.text: Heads of lilies, oxlips, irises, roses and edelweisses or just one flower

indicators.note: heads means the leading letter of each of the flower names that follow

explanation.surface: A bouquet of five kinds of bloom, or perhaps only a single one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' here is a thing that flows, a river: the Loire in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Flower is crossword slang for a river; the Loire is the longest river in France.

clue.text: Fenella, I'm struggling at home

indicators.note: struggling means the letters of these words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A woman named Fenella admits she is finding things hard at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase used in English meaning with one's family, at home informally.

clue.text: Not a novice falling during dance

indicators.note: not means the letters that follow are left out of the falling word

parts.note: L for learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: An experienced dancer avoids tumbling over during a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes A and L from FALLING. L-plates are the signs British learner drivers must display.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland fling is a lively Scottish dance.

clue.text: Dishonest retailer

parts.note: suggests a crooked shopkeeper, but describes someone who retails (retells) untruths

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retailer' is not a shopkeeper: to retail a story is to recount it, and a teller of tales is also a liar.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller of tales, and colloquially a liar who makes things up.
